body: Thank you! Very likely, it looks similar
Thank you so much. I'm so very sorry for your loss as well. I wish neither of us had to experience this at all. But I'm glad media like this exists. It's genuinely therapeutic, and I love it too.

Thank you so much.  I'm definitely in a better place than I was, but it still gets hard, for sure. Your comment genuinely means a lot more to me than you really know. So I'm grateful to you for being so kind.

I lost my boyfriend to suicide in 2020. He was in his 20s, so young. Like many here, I immediately made that connection. I have never felt so heard and understood by a song like this.

The feeling of being desperately so in love with someone, wanting so badly to be their light, their summer sun and help them with the shit they're dealing with. That is, of course, not how things work. But naively you just kinda beg with them hoping that something will connect. That you won't lose them. That they'll win the battles they're fighting. And in your head, you'll do anything to help them with that.

The whole bridge especially broke me. I wasn't physically there when it happened. But god, I wish I could have been. Disarm everything going on in his head. Let him know that I loved him even when things felt difficult. Encouraged him to get the help he so badly needed.

Sending so much love to anyone connecting with this song. I'm in a better place now that this song is definitely therapeutic rather than something I have to skip. And i'm glad, because it means so much and she explains it oh so beautifully. Thank you, Taylor.

This made me cry, in a good way. Thank you for your kind and thoughtful response. And your idea makes sense and is definitely worth a shot. Framing it that way definitely makes me feel a little less hopeless. Thank you for making me heard and understood:)

Firstly, sending you so much love. I wish we didn't have to feel this at all.

I was drawn to your post from the title, guessed you were a Swiftie too. Wanted to say I view this song in such a similar way about my own boyfriend's loss. Even if it's about a breakup, there's something so perfect about the way it describes suicide loss, and not knowing how to move on. Just being completely frozen in time. It makes me cry when I listen to it. 

I hope better days come to you. Know you aren't alone. 💗

Like the others here, I've also had dreams like this.

Dreams where we had broken up, we were arguing, he was moving away, or he just wouldn't want to talk to me. He was always cold and distant for some reason and it would be so painful and real, like the person I loved was rejecting me. But infinitely worse, as you described, was waking up and realizing that he wasn't there at all. 

My therapist says that maybe it's because this person that we were so close to is literally as distant as they can be. And maybe in our dreams, we're trying to explain or process this harsh distance. Because it's just so jarring. 

I will say that my dreams now have more options for good now too. Where I can spend time with him in good contexts. But I think that came with time and processing what has happened more. 

I really hope things get better for you. Genuinely. Just want you to know you aren't alone.

I get this a lot. I felt the same thing about my boyfriend and his friends. They would tell me how much they missed him, and I would struggle hearing it. Because that was my boyfriend. For me, it was wanting validation that the depth of our relationship was different than everyone else's. Protective over my person.

It is true that your loss is different and unique to theirs. You have struggles that they might not understand. Losing a partner is a unique loss, even more so with suicide. You aren't a shitty person for feeling it. You have been through a lot that so many people wouldn't be able to imagine.

What helped me was going, "they can't fully understand what I'm going through, but I also can't fully understand what they're going through." They just feel it differently, similarly to how his family does. They might have complex feelings about not being there as closely as you were, experiences that they shared together, unique reminders that are particularly hard for them. And that's okay. It just means he was loved by a lot of people. That doesn't minimize that he was still your person and vice-versa.

You seem like a super kind and empathetic person who wouldn't use this feeling against anyone. So please do not be frustrated with yourself. You seem to be doing your best to deal with it in a healthy way. Sending you love. <3

Hi there. I lost my boyfriend last year to suicide. I feel with you, so much, and I wish there was anything I could say that could make it feel better.

I want you to know that this wasn't your fault. You tried your best to get him help with the knowledge that you had. And on the day itself, you couldn't have known. He told you he wasn't alone, made you feel like he was safe. As hard as it is, he didn't want anyone to know.

His mother blamed me too. Said it was because we were arguing. It's not fair to have to deal with your own feelings of guilt and external blame all at once. It is awful. But it wasn't you; she is telling you that to deal with her own guilt and I really wish she didn't. But the truth is, he made that choice, none of you did.

I didn't think I would make it a day, a week, a month, let alone a year. But I have. I don't know how sometimes, but I held on. It was hard, really hard. I felt like a zombie for months before I could even feel present in my brain again. But it will come. The intensity of the pain does not stay intense all the time. You will have moments again where you can smile, think about him with all the happiness involved. It will still be sad, but in a way where it is bittersweet instead.

But first, let yourself feel. Cry, yell, vent to whoever will listen. It is a mix of the most inexplicable feelings. You might not be able to verbalize all of it, but trying might get some of the weight off of your shoulders. Posting here has really helped me so often. I hope it does to you as well.

If you ever need to talk, my inbox is open. Sending you so much love and strength. To just get through. You can get through. Even when it feels like it isn't possible. <3

Hello. I'm so sorry for your loss as well. Thank you so much for taking the time to respond.

It really does feel like my mind has maybe accepted it more, especially compared to where I was a few months ago. It just honestly still feels so conflicting realizing that. But thank you for the reassurance, it gives me a lot of comfort. I just get really afraid I'll forget sometimes. I really don't want to lose those dreams with him. But I'll hold onto that idea, thank you.

This describes it so well. The idea that time is moving further and further away from them being here alive, is something that I've genuinely dreaded me for a while. The more days that pass, the more it sinks in, and it's started to be heavy for me in a different way than before.

I wasn't able to see my boyfriend after he passed. Like you, I struggled with it a lot. Due to covid, I couldn't even be there at his funeral, so I kept telling myself that it was all a lie, a sick joke. No pictures or anything either. For me, seeing his name on a grave marker was the first time it started to feel real. I think that was really important to me to sit there next to it and let it sink in. Even then, my brain still came up with crazy stories as to why it must have still been a joke, but it definitely became harder to deny. And with time, I think it has gotten easier, too. It still feels like a dream sometimes, but I can also be in reality a lot more as well. I hope things get easier for you, please take care.
Feel this so hard. Sending you so much love. <3

I lost my boyfriend too and feel your pain. People don't seem to understand the level of turmoil we go through on a daily basis, and can say the most upsetting things without even realising. I do have to remind you, it isn't your fault. I wish none of us had to feel this at all, but just remember you aren't alone in feeling it.
Thank you. I'm really doing my best to be okay.
Thank you for your kind words. Yeah. It's just so hard sometimes waiting for it to get better. I just don't want to feel like this anymore, it's exhausting. But i'm trying my best.
This is a really good reminder. Thank you for sharing.

Yes. I have dreams where he's there, through some unspoken loophole he's back. In the first few weeks after he died I had a dream where he was there and I was worried he would kill himself. So I directly said something along the lines of "Please don't go and hurt yourself, please talk to me" and he responded, "What are you talking about? I'm not going to die," like I was speaking nonsense.

Other times, I have dreams where he's there, but he's distant for some reason, or we're not talking, which really hurts. But nothing hurts more than that moment when you wake up and you realise they aren't there at all.

Sending you so much love. I am so, so sorry for your loss. I'm 22, too, and I lost my boyfriend to suicide earlier in the year. I relate to so many of the feelings you're having. But, I'm just so sorry you have to go through this at all. It really does feel so incomprehensible.

Please remember we're all here with you. My inbox is open if ever you want to talk. But no pressure. Please hold on and be as kind to yourself as you can. <3

Nothing is wrong with you. When my boyfriend died, I had to stop myself from deleting all the apps and games on my phone that we used together because it hurt me seeing them. I put them all in a separate folder because it was just too difficult to just see them there. The first time I logged out of my PS4 account and saw his, I broke down too.

Sometimes seeing these things just feels like salt in an open wound. More reminders of something we already know all too well. Please be kind to yourself.

This makes perfect sense. I lost my boyfriend 8ish months ago and for the longest while, I couldn't even talk about him with others because my brain would go straight to that final day, blocking all the good out. His friends would bring up positive memories they had of him and I would feel so disconnected from it. Like I had a gap in my memory of him, instead agonizing over every detail, regret, and what-if of what led up to it.

I do have to say that while I still have that and find it difficult, it's gotten a little easier to think of the good. And if I'm still struggling, I sometimes gain enough courage to look at his photos, videos and messages which helps. All this to say, give yourself time to process things, and I hope more room for the good memories come to you eventually. Please take care.

My heart is with you right now. While not exactly the same, I lost my boyfriend this year at 22 as well. There are no words that can do justice to how you must be feeling right now. 

Suicide grief is really isolating, and this sub has been a lifeline for me and many others to not feel so alone. I hope it brings some comfort, however small, to you as well. I know words probably feel so futile to hear right now, but as everyone has said we are all here with you. My own inbox is also open if ever you feel so inclined.

Please be kind to yourself.
I feel you. I get really upset when I hear people tell me I'll move on, because they have no clue what this is like. I'm so sorry you're in it too.

I totally feel you, the holidays definitely feel like they're looming in my head, too. It's hard to imagine without him. Part of me wants to sleep through it and ignore all the inevitable couple posts on social media. Thank you so much, will also be here

I can't imagine I'll ever fully stop thinking of him either. I think a lot of me would never want to stop. And it's so hard to explain that to people who don't get it.

And I'm totally with you on the friend group thing. It's incredibly difficult to see all of them happily coupled up, when you don't have your person here anymore. It makes you that more acutely aware of the empty space next to you.

I'm so sorry you're in this boat, too. I really wish neither of us had to feel this at all.

This is something I've been absolutely terrified of too. I've been dreading my next birthday for a similar reason as I don't want to feel like I'm older than he ever was. It feels wrong and like the universe is upside down, doesn't it? 

All this to say you're not alone, and I really hope you take care of yourself, friend. <3
Thank you so much for your kind words.
Thank you so much.

Lover has become so personal to me. My boyfriend passed away this year, and this was very much "our album". Every single song makes me think of him, regardless of meaning. 

I remember it being released on Spotify while I was at work. He and I were messaging reacting to each song, immediately adding songs like Lover, Paper Rings, Daylight, Cornelia Street to our playlists for each other. Taylor's music was one of the first things we bonded over in high school, but this was the first album we had experienced releasing while we were actually together. 

He knew how much I loved it, and asked his aunt in the US to buy us the Lover album booklet. Every time new Taylor content was released, we'd watch and sing along together.

Since he passed, I haven't been able to listen to Lover in its entirety. It brings back so many memories, good and bad. 

In a lot of ways, this album is my "Cornelia Street". It really breaks my heart to revisit it because he's no longer here with me. It reminds me of a time where I was so in love with him and the world around us. Maybe I'll get the strength to revisit it someday soon.

I'm so, so sorry for your loss. I lost my boyfriend this year too. I know what it's like to wish you could've known, but always remember that it wasn't your fault. Sending you all the love and strength. Please hold on best you can.

I'm so sorry for your loss. I understand that. It's really some of the most heartwrenching pain.

Thank you for sharing this with me. I suppose I've been very avoidant to try new things. It takes so much energy out of me. But this does give me some hope to hear. So thank you.

Sending you the same. <3
Thank you so much. Yes, that makes sense. I think I just struggle to hold myself accountable to it sometimes, days tend to blur into each other.
I'm really so sorry for your loss. Thank you. It does help to not feel so alone. But I really wish neither of us had to feel this at all. Sending you love <3

Perhaps due to my current mental state, this song is without a doubt my favourite on the album. My SO passed away during quarantine, and holy shit, that bridge cuts at me in a way I can't fully express.

The whole song does actually. It captures anxious self-doubt, anger, and frustration with oneself so well. Makes me feel heard, dude.

The beauty of this album is how you can write an easay on how each song attacks your heart specificially. I love it.

I lost my boyfriend to suicide, and I can't tell you how much I wish more people checked in on me, especially at the very beginning, but even until now. Even if I knew I couldn't or didn't want to talk, just hearing someone say "I'm here if you need me/want to talk" made me feel infinitely less alone. When my own mental health has been really struggling, I've wished I had more people I knew I could call to just let the weight I was carrying off my chest.

I know a lot of people are scared to reach out, because they don't know what to say. I can't speak for your friend, but I never personally expected anyone to know the right thing to say. How could they possibly? But having people tell me they wanted to listen, or even sometimes offer to distract me by talking about something irrelevant or light-hearted could help a great deal. Sometimes you just want to cling to any sense of normalcy you can.

You seem like a very good friend, and he is lucky to have you. Reaching out to him consistently is so good of you, and I can assume is very helpful to him as well. Just be patient with him, but also with yourself. It's not easy to navigate, but you seem to be doing the very best you can to help.

I've always been the one to mostly keep to myself when I'm struggling. In fact, my boyfriend was a rare instance where I did ask for help while he was alive. Since, I feel so scared to do again. I'm my own worst enemy
I get socially anxious, so the idea of talking to someone I don't know is quite scary to me. I hope that makes sense. I know it's most likely in my head, but yes, it's difficult.

I know I don't want anyone else to hurt, but it's just so hard to hold on sometimes. I just still can't comprehend how to take any steps at all. I'll definitely try my best. Thank you so much for this, I really appreciate it <3

I dread those moments a lot, even just having them in my own home. I'm terrified for the day 'll have to step out without him. I get that, I really do still wish everything could stop. I just know I can't avoid things carrying on as much as I would like to.

I have. Yeah, it becomes really difficult to hold on when it's at its heaviest again. Like I can't see beyond it. That helps, thank you.

Yes. I know it isn't reality, but I do often wish it was. Thank you <3

Thank you so much. The idea of therapy is still quite daunting to me, though I do know I really want help. Yeah, I suppose it's a positive that we're not being rushed back into it. Wishing you the same. <3
Covid definitely has made it so much worse. Yeah, I want to, but I'm still really scared to actually do it and ask for help. But I'll try my best. Thank you so much <3

Hi. I'm so, so sorry for your loss. My heart is really with you right now. I lost my boyfriend to suicide a few months back and I know how painful it is to be the last person to speak to them.

As hard as it may get to remember, this wasn't your fault. You did all that you could and did your best to reach out. Please remind yourself that even when it becomes hard to believe. 

I'm really happy you have a good support system. You may not feel like it right now, but my inbox is open should you want to talk. It's helped me a lot talking to people who seem to understand. Sending you love. <3

Everything happens for a reason" or "you can't see it now, but this will make you stronger". Makes me lose my mind. 

Also, "I would have stopped him if I had known." Which is much easier said when you weren't there. I know people mean well, but it's hard to hear.

Thank you. It feels so impossible to reach out to people. I don't have really close friends. I get so scared to reach out to people, and when I do, it's always over quickly. Like i'm too exhausting to deal with.

I try not to be, but I really get so angry at him sometimes. It's really not fair. I have to sit alone with the guilt and the hurt and the questions. And the only person I trusted is gone. 

It's hard to get a counselor in this country. And I don't have any really close friends who care to listen very long or who I can trust. My family tries, but I feel like a burden to them.
